question: Last year (2023), marked the first year of implementation of the new Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The new framework for 2023-2027 centres on10 key objectives that are linked to EU goals for social, environmental and economic sustainability in agriculture and rural areas. It also significantly changes the way in which subsidies are granted and places an emphasis on results and performance.

The climate crisis and the continuous rise in production costs seen in recent years because of the pandemic, the war in Ukraine, the energy crisis, etc., are putting enormous pressure on the farming community. This situation triggered the mass protests recently staged by farmers across the EU, as the farming community is unable to fulfil all obligations laid down in the new CAP. In view of this: 1.
Does the Commission intend to review, amend and simplify the provisions of the new CAP and, if so, when?
Does it intend to make targeted adjustments to help farmers by easing the transition towards the new regulatory requirements, with appropriate measures to support them and, if so, when?
answer: A proposal for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) post-2027 is expected to be presented in 2025 under the new College. In the meantime, the Commission has proposed to change certain provisions (1) of the current CAP related to conditionality and CAP Strategic Plans which are currently being considered by the European Parliament and the Council in the context of the ordinary legislative procedure.

At the same time, the Commission presented to the Agriculture and Fisheries (AGRIFISH) Council of 26 March 2024 a nonpaper detailing a number of possible actions to strengthen the position of farmers in the supply chain in the short and mediumlong term (2).
